what_happened: The job to make drain and status never skip a dispatched job with no outcome was rejected at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: the criterion that six named earlier jobs each end with an outcome record (finished, resumed or closed with a reason), with closed jobs whose work landed citing the commit hash from git log and the others re-queued. That criterion was checked against the live records. There was one major finding and no blockers: 4 of the 6 named jobs (20261027-054148-g63s, 20261027-123701-77zh, 20261027-054206-w1y3, 20261027-054209-z7sj) still have no outcome record, and the two that are closed do not cite a commit hash. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: One criterion required a cleanup of live records. The code diff cannot show that, and nothing in the producer's flow tied the cleanup to a stage that must complete and report it. The reading mixed a code change (drain and status never skip) with a one-time data repair of six named jobs. The producer was not required to list each job and its resulting record, and nothing cross-checked the live records against the criterion before the final verdict. So the data half was left undone and was found only by the verifier. The fit to the chosen class is loose: this is an unmet criterion on record state, not a misread reading.
prevention: Add a code check that runs before the final verdict. For a job whose criteria name specific job ids, the check reads the live records and lists, per id, whether an outcome record exists and whether a closed job cites a commit hash found in git log. It reports any gap to the producer while it can still act. The code fix and the one-time record repair should also be separate deliverables, each with its own evidence.
proposed_request: Give each of these six dispatched jobs an outcome record: 20261026-232359-msh3, 20261026-232423-hvyb, 20261027-054148-g63s, 20261027-123701-77zh, 20261027-054206-w1y3 and 20261027-054209-z7sj. For each one, check git log for its work. If the work landed, close the job with a reason that cites the commit hash. If it did not land, re-queue it. Two of these jobs are already closed without a commit hash, so add the hash to their records. When done, list each job with its outcome and the hash or new job id. Do not change drain or status code in this job, because that part is already done.
